summary: cql-write at QUORUM: local apply on n1, MUTATION_REQ to n2 and n3, parallel join returns at blockFor 2; replicas append to the commit log and write the memtable for shop.users.
n3 down: should-hint passes, one hint submitted before the sends, do-verb only to n2, success with 2 acks.
Two down: unavailable 0x1000 (required 2, alive 1) from assure-sufficient-live-replicas; nothing sent, nothing hinted.

Both remotes hang: write-timeout 0x1100, received 1 of 2, SIMPLE, at 2000ms (was 4082ms in round 1); both hinted at callback expiry (t >= 2000). Round 1 sim-gap resolved by parallel join and handler deadline.
ONE with n3 hanging: client answer before 200ms; n3 hinted late after 2000ms. Round 1 sim-gap resolved.
Round 1 correction confirmed (coordinator must not be a replica; four-node-rf3, token -100). ANY: one HintRunnable for n2, n3, n4 is the single ack; nothing sent.
ALL with n2 down: unavailable (required 3, alive 2) before any send.
Replica n2: commit-log.add before the memtable write, MUTATION_RSP with no fsync wait; with the last sync 20s old (> 15000ms lag block) the writer waits for a sync first.

Flush switches, writes an sstable, makes it live, then discards only unused segment files (mixed and allocating segments kept). But the sstable carries no partitions and switch-out keeps the memtable cells, so a read after flush is served from the memtable (bench-w9-readback fails on purpose); and archive-and-discard deletes segments from an active_segments counter regardless of dirtiness.

daemon-startup replays seeded segments: persisted entry skipped, two entries applied without the commit log, flushed, file deleted, all before init-server and native-transport start. Round 1 partial fixed (replay now lists segments from state).
